intro: HTML to PDF turns a web page stored on your computer into a PDF document. Use it to keep a report generated by an application, an invoice or an email exported as HTML, a project's documentation or a page you designed yourself, and get a file that looks and prints the same everywhere.

You can upload a single HTML file or a ZIP with the page and its assets: stylesheets, images, fonts and SVG. In a ZIP, the main page is index.html, or the least deeply nested HTML file if there is none with that name, and relative paths to other files in the ZIP are resolved even when they sit in subfolders. Hidden files and the __MACOSX folder that Macs add are ignored. Each ZIP produces the PDF of a single main page.

Chromium does the conversion on our server, in an environment with no internet connection. Images, stylesheets, fonts or scripts that the page requests from other sites are not loaded, so anything not included in the ZIP or embedded in the HTML itself will be missing from the PDF. Scripts included in the page or the ZIP do run. To save a page published on the internet from its address, use Web to PDF.

Choose the paper (A3, A4, A5, Letter or Legal), the orientation and the margins, from 0 to 50 mm. Under more options you decide whether background colours and images are printed, whether all the content goes on one long page, whether the print or the screen styles are applied, and whether the page size set in the CSS with @page is respected. With several files you get one PDF for each and a ZIP with all of them; the maximum number of pages depends on your plan.
steps: Upload an HTML file or a ZIP with the page and its assets.
Choose the paper, orientation and margins.
Download the PDF of each page or the ZIP with all of them.

faq.q: Why are some images or the page's font missing?
faq.a: They are most likely loaded from the internet, and the conversion has no connection. Download those files, put them in a ZIP next to the HTML with relative paths and convert it again.

faq.q: What is the difference between the print and screen media types?
faq.a: Many pages have their own print styles that hide menus or change colours. "Print" uses those styles; "Screen" shows the page as it looks in the browser.

faq.q: Can I convert several HTML pages that link to each other?
faq.a: Each ZIP produces the PDF of its main page. Upload each page in its own ZIP or as a separate file and combine them afterwards with Merge PDF.
